_meta.what: Battle Brothers combat rules as numbers, every value carrying its wiki page and an exact quote. Reference only: describes Battle Brothers' own hex board; Bohemia's square grid and house tiles are separate locked rulings.

sources.CORE_WIKITEXT.md: reference/library/grok/wiki/CORE_WIKITEXT.md (its '# PAGE Combat_Mechanics' is byte-identical in body to bb_all/0424_Combat Mechanics.txt)

_meta.quote_rule: Each quote is a verbatim substring of its source (whitespace collapsed); wiki markup is kept where it sits inside the quoted span.

wiki_caveat.value: Some weapons' parameters, skills, perks have not been updated since 'Blazing Deserts' (2020) and 'Of Flesh and Faith' (2022) DLCs.
wiki_caveat.quote: Some weapons' parameters, skills, perks have not been updated since 'Blazing Deserts' (2020) and 'Of Flesh and Faith' (2022) DLCs.

conflicts: Thrown-weapon base accuracy: Combat Mechanics says +30, Hit Chance says +20 (Throw Axe/Bola/Javelin/Spear). Both kept under hit_chance.ranged.distance.thrown.
Thrown-weapon first hex: Combat Mechanics says thrown weapons DO count the first hex; Hit Chance gives one formula (distance - 1) for every skill. Both kept.
Hit roll comparison: Combat Mechanics says 'lower than'; Hit Chance gives 'hit roll <= hit chance'. Both kept under hit_chance.roll.
Height: Combat Mechanics gives a flat +10/-10; Hit Chance gives +10 for being higher and -10 'per level difference' for being lower. Both kept.

grid.quote: The battlefield is a hex-tiled grid, with elevation, obstacles/terrain considerations and zone of control mechanics.

height_levels.quote: Flat Ground (0 Height Level) [[File:Height 0.png]] * 1. Height Level [[File:Height 1.png]] * 2. Height Level [[File:Height 2.png]] * 3. Height Level [[File:Height 3.png]]

searched: grep of all 2255 bb_all pages for '<n> x <n>', 'map size', 'battlefield size', 'tiles wide', 'hexes wide'
battlefield_size_hexes.note: No page in the dump gives the battle map's dimensions in hexes. Closest statements quoted below.

nearest.quote: The game is balanced around skirmish-level infantry combat in terms of map size, game mechanics and skills.
The battlefield is too large for him to rally everyone, but a squad can deploy more than one Standard Bearer.

max_fielded_per_side_player.quote: The player starts the game with 3 men, will [[Character_Backgrounds|hire]] more from settlements (up to 20) and can field a maximum of 12 men in battles.

vision_default.quote: Commonly, a hired mercenary has a Vision value of 7.

vision_floor.quote: Vision cannot be reduced below 1. Elevation is taken into account after the cap

min_gap_between_lines_hexes.quote: A typical battle starts with both parties in a line formation (1-2 lines deep for your forces, may be deeper for the enemy), with at least 5 hexes between parties.

player_lines_deep.quote: 1-2 lines deep for your forces, may be deeper for the enemy

no_melee_closing_round_one.quote: Human forces cannot close to melee distance within 1 round as traversing a hex takes a minimum of 2AP.

ranged_in_range_round_one.quote: As bows have a range of 7 tiles on the flat (8 with mastery) and crossbows have a range of 6 tiles, both sides start the 1st round within firing distance of ranged combatants.

player_deployment_phase.note: Dev posts only call a pre-battle deployment phase 'planned'; no rule stated.

nearest.quote: A pre-battle formation setup or deployment phase is a planned feature. It won't be available when you're ambushed, though.

retreat_from_map_edge.value: men on the edge retreat safely; others auto-move to the edge with a ZoC defense bonus scaled by difficulty
retreat_from_map_edge.quote: If your men are already on the edges of the map, you’ll safely retreat as before. If they aren’t, they’ll now attempt to speedily move to the edges of the map automatically and by themselves until either they succeed or die. While this is going on, they’ll get a defense bonus for moving through zones of control, the amount of which scales with the chosen difficulty level.

per_turn.quote: All brothers and most enemy units have 9AP.

per_turn_exceptions.quote: A few have less (ie Wiedergangers) and some have more (ie Direwolves, Goblin Wolfriders).

refresh.quote: AP is spent by actions (moving, striking, using special skills/consumables, etc) and refreshed at the start of the every round.

refresh_exceptions.quote: Action Points fully recover every round unless a unit is stunned or affected by goblin poison or by a certain injury.

turn_ends_at_zero.quote: When AP reach 0, the turn for the character ends, and the next unit acts

rough.quote: Rough terrain such as Forest/Snow have tiles that typically cost 3AP (there are tiles that still cost 2AP though (ie Light Snow)).

murky_water_swamp.quote: Swamp costs 4AP for tiles with Murky Water.

height_change_extra.quote: Changing elevation adds a further +1 to AP cost per tile.

pathfinder.quote: Action Point costs for movement on all terrain is reduced by -1 to a minimum of 2[[File:Action_points.png|25px|bottom]] Action Points per tile, and [[File:Fatigue.png|25px|bottom]] Fatigue cost is reduced to half. Changing height levels has no additional [[File:Action_points.png|25px|bottom]] Action Point cost anymore, but [[File:Fatigue.png|25px|bottom]] Fatigue cost is unaffected.

one_handed.quote: Most strikes from 1-handed weapons use 4AP (exception: Dagger (with Mastery) uses only 3AP)

two_handed.quote: strikes from 2-handed weapons use 6AP (exception: Warbrand, Rhomphaia and 2-Handed Cleavers use 4AP on regular strikes; Jagged Pike uses 5AP).

two_handed_exceptions.quote: exception: Warbrand, Rhomphaia and 2-Handed Cleavers use 4AP on regular strikes; Jagged Pike uses 5AP

action_needs_fatigue.value: a fully fatigued character can neither strike nor move
action_needs_fatigue.quote: Apart from AP, all weapon strikes and movement on the battlefield also cost fatigue to execute, therefore a fully fatigued character can neither strike nor move.

recovery_per_turn.quote: Every character recovers 15 fatigue at the start of his turn.

recovery_per_turn_attributes.quote: Fatigue recovers for a basic amount of 15 every round.

on_dodge_or_block.quote: dodging/blocking blows also increases Fatigue by 2 and getting struck by a blow increases Fatigue by 5.

on_dodge_or_block_scope.value: melee only; dodging/blocking ranged attacks builds none
on_dodge_or_block_scope.quote: Dodging or blocking melee attacks with a shield builds up 2 Fatigue points. Some enemies’ attacks build up more Fatigue on targets they hit (e.g. [[Fallen Hero]]es deal double fatigue damage, as well as [[Armored Wiederganger]]s after day 20). Dodging or blocking ranged attacks does not incur Fatigue build-up.

on_struck.quote: getting struck by a blow increases Fatigue by 5.

on_struck_by_mace.quote: Being hit by melee or ranged weapon builds up 5 Fatigue, 10 and 20 if hit by one- and two-handed maces respectively.

orc_gear_extra_per_skill_for_humans.quote: also build up additional 5 Fatigue points for every skill when used by humans.

initiative_penalty.value: current initiative = initiative - accumulated fatigue - penalty to max fatigue from gear
initiative_penalty.quote: The average Battle Brother has a value around 100, which is reduced by the current fatigue as well as any penalty to maximum fatigue (such as from heavy armor and weapons, other equipment).

initiative_penalty_one_for_one_confirmed.quote: At all times your [[File:Initiative.png|25px|bottom]] Initiative is reduced only by 50% of your accumulated [[File:Fatigue.png|25px|bottom]] Fatigue, instead of all of it.
initiative_penalty_one_for_one_confirmed.note: Relentless halves it, so the default is 100% of accumulated fatigue.

bag_items_penalty_multiplier.quote: although this penalty is reduced by 50% while said items are in your bags

searched: grep of all bb_all pages for 'fatigue per tile', terrain words near 'fatigue'
move_fatigue_per_terrain.note: The wiki says moving and changing height cost fatigue, and Pathfinder halves it, but no page gives the per-terrain fatigue numbers.

nearest.quote: Changing height level costs more action points and costs more fatigue than walking on the same height layer.

recover_perk.quote: which allows to reduce accumulated [[File:Fatigue.png|bottom|25px]] Fatigue by 50% by resting for the current turn (costs 9[[File:Action_points.png|25px|Action Points|bottom]]).

order.value: highest initiative acts first each round
order.quote: The character with the highest initiative will start first in a battle round, followed by characters with lower initiative.

fatigue_moves_you_back.quote: As initiative is lowered when a character builds up fatigue or has a penalty to max. fatigue (due to armor/weapons or other effects), his turn may move from first to last very quickly, if he gets fatigued too fast and the enemies do not.

average_brother.quote: The average Battle Brother has a value around 100

wait_penalty_next_round.quote: Changed the waiting action to reduce initiative by 25% for the purpose of determining turn order the following turn. This is to lessen the problem of taking double-turns, i.e. two turns in quick succession.

wait_penalty_relentless_removes.quote: Using the 'Wait' command no longer gives you a −25% penalty to [[File:Initiative.png|25px|bottom]] Initiative when determining the turn order on the next round.

wait_acts_later_same_round.note: Waiting moving a unit to later in the current round is implied by a dev post, not stated as a rule.

nearest.quote: If a character would have already spent most of their AP and then waited, in essence already having concluded their turn save for 2 AP or so, and then get stunned, they’d lose that same turn at the end of the round which they already acted on.

skip_round_button.value: all men skip their turns for the current round
skip_round_button.quote: Clicking it (or using the hotkey) and confirming your choice in the following dialog will have all your men skip their turns for the current round.

fleeing_turn_order.quote: is also instantly moved to the end of turn order. At the start of a round Fleeing units have a penalty of -1000 initiative for turn order only, so they will act last

adrenaline.note: Status lasts 1 turn; 'The bonus initiative only counts towards the turn order.'

adrenaline_tiebreak.value: highest initiative among Adrenaline users first
adrenaline_tiebreak.quote: if two characters are using [[File:Perk_37_active.png|25px|bottom]] [[Adrenaline (20 fatigue)|Adrenaline skill]], the one with the highest [[File:Initiative.png|25px|bottom]] Initiative will act first.

who_exerts.value: melee units: melee weapon, bare fists, or beasts (except alps and hexes)
who_exerts.quote: Melee units - units with a melee weapon, bare fists, or beasts (except for alps and hexes) - exert a Zone of Control on tiles directly adjacent to them.

radius_hexes.quote: exert a Zone of Control on tiles directly adjacent to them.

free_attacks_on_leave.quote: Any unit trying to leave a tile under Zone of Control will suffer automatic strikes from the hostiles controlling the ZoC (at no fatigue cost for the controlling unit).

leave_resolution.value: all miss = leaves; any hit = stays and must try again
leave_resolution.quote: If all strikes miss, the unit leaves the tile. If any strike hits, the attempt to leave the tile fails and the unit has to try again.

no_zoc.quote: A unit using any kind of ranged weapon (i.e. bow, javelins), a fleeing or stunned unit does not exert a Zone of Control. A smoke pot removes the ZoC from affected tiles for 1 turn.

no_zoc_more.quote: Entangled, horrified, and sleeping units lose their ability to exert their ZoC.

bypass.quote: Footwork skill allows to move through ZoC safely. Rotation skill allows a unit to leave the ZoC by swapping positions with another non-hostile unit.

height_gap_breaks_zoc_levels.quote: If there are two or more levels of height difference between the hex a character is standing on and an enemy in an adjacent hex, you do not count as being in melee attack range or being in each other's Zone of Control.

base_melee.quote: Base chance to hit (shown after selecting a skill and mousing over a target) is essentially: melee skill of brother subtracted against base melee defense of target.

main_formula.value: hit chance = skill - defense; skill = skill * skill multiplier; defense = defense * defense multiplier
main_formula.quote: hit chance = skill - defense With: skill = skill * skill multiplier defense = defense * defense multiplier

additive_vs_multiplicative.quote: Gear, elevation and surround bonuses are factored in additively. (ie an attacker with Melee Skill of 70 striking a defender with Melee Defense of 0 will have 70% hit chance. If said attacker had another friendly unit adjacent/surrounding the defender, he would get +5% or in other words his hit chance would be 75% instead) *Morale bonuses/penalties and injury penalties are factored in multiplicatively

defense_soft_cap_cm.quote: each Melee Defense attribute point over 50 is halved.

per_extra_adjacent.quote: For each unit after the first surrounding, a bonus of +5% melee hit chance is given to allies attacking the surrounded target.

formula.value: melee defense = melee defense - surround bonus * (adjacent enemies - 1)
formula.quote: melee defense = melee defense - surround bonus * (adjacent enemies - 1)

applies_to_non_adjacent_melee_attackers.quote: Gunther is not adjacent to the surrounded [[Humans#Brigands|Raider]] and attacks him with a [[Longaxe]]. He will also benefit from a bonus of +10% hit chance

not_ranged.quote: Bernhard will not benefit from any bonus because he is using a [[Ranged Weapons|Ranged Weapon]].

not_contributing.quote: [[Stunned (Status Effect)|Stunned]] brothers or brothers with [[Ranged Weapons]] will not contribute to surround bonus.

backstabber.quote: The bonus to hitchance in melee is doubled to +10% for each ally

underdog.value: negates surround malus; vs Backstabber normal malus applies
underdog.quote: The defense malus due to being surrounded by opponents no longer applies to this character. If an attacker has the Backstabber perk, the effect of that perk is negated, and the normal defense malus due to being surrounded is applied instead.

higher_attacker_bonus.quote: When standing on a higher height level than your opponent, you gain a +10% chance to hit and they suffer a -10% penalty to hit.

lower_attacker_penalty.quote: they suffer a -10% penalty to hit.

hit_chance_page_wording.quote: If the attacker is on a tile that's more elevated than his target's a +10% bonus to hit chance is granted. If the attacker is on a tile that is below his target's a −10% penalty to hit chance per level difference is applied.

melee_max_height_gap.quote: You only count as being in melee attack range if there is a one level difference of height between opposing characters standing in adjacent hexes.

ranged_range_per_level.quote: Ranged weapons gain an additional hex of range for each level of height and improved hit chance versus targets at a lower height level.

base.quote: to-hit = Ranged Skill of brother subtracted by base Ranged Defense of target.

distance_formula.value: hit chance + (distance to target - 1) * hit chance per tile modifier
distance_formula.quote: hit chance = hit chance + (distance to target - 1) * hit chance per tile modifier

bow_quick_shot.quote: Regular [[bows]] suffer -4% accuracy per hex with [https://battlebrothers.fandom.com/wiki/Skills#Weapon_Skills Quickshot] (no base accuracy bonus)

bow_aimed_shot.quote: Regular [[bows]] suffer -2% accuracy per hex with [https://battlebrothers.fandom.com/wiki/Skills#Weapon_Skills Aimed Shot] (offset by a +10% base accuracy bonus)

crossbow_shoot_bolt.quote: [[Crossbows]] suffer -3% accuracy per hex when using the [https://battlebrothers.fandom.com/wiki/Skills#Weapon_Skills Shoot Bolt] skill (offset by +15% base accuracy bonus for the Shoot Bolt skill (only +10% base accuracy bonus if using a [[Spiked Impaler]]))

thrown.quote: Thrown weapons (e.g. [[Bundle of Javelins]]) suffer a penalty of -10% accuracy per hex (offset by a +30% base accuracy bonus). Note that, unlike bows and crossbows, thrown weapons DO count the first hex from the attacker for distance effects on accuracy.

first_hex_not_counted_bows_crossbows.quote: The first hex from the bowman is NOT counted and does not give penalties for the purposes of to-hit chance calculations.

worked_example_aimed.quote: Aimed Shot] by a Ranged Skill 50 bowman on a [[Humans|Bandit Thug]] with a Ranged Defense skill of 0 who is 7 hexes away, will have 50% + 10% (Aimed Shot) - 12% (accuracy degradation of 2 for 6 hexes of distance) = 48% to-hit chance.

cover_line_of_fire_blocked.quote: reduces overall to-hit chance by 75%. This penalty can be reduced to 50% by the [https://battlebrothers.fandom.com/wiki/Perks#bullseye Bullseye] perk.

cover_hit_chance_page.quote: The base hit chance penalty to reach a blocked target is 75%. The Bullseye Perk reduces it to 50% (* 0.66). If this fails the shot goes astray. One among the intended target obstacles is randomly chosen and targeted instead. If the shot goes astray a −15% penalty to hit chance is applied. Attacks made over allies at a range of 2 tiles are not blocked.

cover_bullseye.quote: The penalty to hit chance when shooting at a target that has no clear line of fire is reduced from 75% to 50% for ranged weapons.

scatter.quote: Projectiles that miss a target (intended or not) at a distance > 2 tiles can scatter and hit adjacent targets. For attackers other than the player the chance is 25% but no ally must be adjacent to the target.

scatter_beyond_range.quote: Ranged attacks via the scatter mechanic can actually strike unintended targets one hex beyond the normal maximum range of the attack in question.

combat_mechanics.quote: Battles fought during the night give combatants the [[Nighttime (Status Effect)|'''''Nighttime''''']] debuff which gives them penalties of -2 Vision, -30% Ranged Skill and -30% Ranged Defense

cap.quote: Hit chance for regular attacks cannot be lower than 5% and cannot go higher than 95%. hit chance = max(5, min(95, hit chance))

utility_auto_hit.quote: Utility skills will always hit. hit chance = 100

roll.value: d100 1..100; hit if roll <= hit chance
roll.quote: hit roll = rand(1, 100) hit = hit roll <= hit chance

roll_cm_wording.value: d100; hit if roll lower than hit chance
roll_cm_wording.quote: When an attack is made, a regular d100 roll happens (a procedure to get a random number in the range of 1 to 100). If the number is lower than the to-hit % chance, then this is a hit.

beginner_difficulty_roll_shift.quote: player hit roll = hit roll - 5 enemy hit roll = hit roll +5

lucky_reroll.quote: 10% chance to require the attacker to make 2 successful attack rolls to hit you

morale_example.quote: an archer with 86 Ranged Skill at Steady will have effectively 94 Ranged Skill at Confident (+10%)

terrain_swamp.quote:
-25% [[File:Melee_skill.png|25px|Melee Skill]]
-25% [[File:Melee_defense.png|25px|Melee Defense]]
-25% [[File:Ranged_defense.png|25px|Ranged Defense]]

dodge_perk.quote: Gain 15% of the character's current Initiative as a bonus to Melee and Ranged Defense.

shieldwall.quote: can be used in combat to double shield defense (inclusive of Shield Expert bonus) with a additional +5 bonus for each adjacent ally also using the

shields.note: [melee defense, ranged defense]; full table rows in the source, quote is the Buckler cell.

head_roll_is_second_d100.quote: At this point, a second d100 roll is made to see if it the attack hits the head.

head_hit_is_critical.quote: If the head is hit the hit is a critical hit and will do additional [[damage]].

head_chance_formula.value: chance to hit head * chance to hit head multiplier
head_chance_formula.quote: critical hit chance = chance to hit head * chance to hit head multiplier

head_chance_bonuses.quote: |Reach melee weapons |5 |- |Two-handed swords (all) |5 |- |One-handed Flails (all) |10 |- |Two-handed Flails (all) |15 |- |Throwing Axes |5

head_damage_cm.quote: if critical hit, everything is multiplied by 1.5: HP damage = HP damage * 1.5

head_extra_hp_only.quote: Hits on the head are called '''critical hits''' and inflict 50% more [[File:Health.png|25px|bottom]]HP damage.

steel_brow.note: Sets body damage multiplier received to 1 (no critical bonus).

value.armor_damage: base damage * modifiers * effectiveness against armor %
value.hp_damage: base damage * modifiers * ignoring armor damage % - armor * 0.1
value.if_armor_destroyed_add: base damage * modifiers * (1 - ignoring armor damage %) - armor damage you already did (cannot be negative)

simplified_formula.quote: armor damage = base damage * modifiers * effectiveness against armor % 1. HP damage = base damage * modifiers * ignoring armor damage % - armor * 0.1 2. if armor = 0 (destroyed), more damage is added (cannot be negative): + base damage * modifiers * (1 - ignoring armor damage %) - armor damage you already did 3. if critical hit, everything is multiplied by 1.5: HP damage = HP damage * 1.5

two_rolls.value: armor and HP damage rolled separately

regular_damage_dealt.value: rand(min, max) * regular damage multiplier * damage multiplier
regular_damage_dealt.quote: = rand(min regular damage, max regular damage) * regular damage multiplier * damage multiplier

armor_damage_dealt.value: rand(min, max) * armor damage multiplier * damage multiplier
armor_damage_dealt.quote: = rand(min regular damage, max regular damage) * armor damage multiplier * damage multiplier

armor_damage_received.value: min(armor, armor damage dealt * armor damage multiplier * damage multiplier)
armor_damage_received.quote: = min( armor, armor damage (dealt) * armor damage multiplier * damage multiplier)

hp_damage_received.value: (regular * direct dealt * direct mult - armor * 0.1 [+ if armor destroyed or direct==1: regular * (1 - direct dealt * direct mult) - armor damage]) * body damage multiplier; no step negative; floor at skill's minimum damage
hp_damage_received.quote: = (regular damage * direct damage (dealt) * direct damage multiplier - armor * armor direct damage mitigation multiplier and if armor is destroyed or direct damage (dealt) = 1 + regular damage * (1 - direct damage (dealt) * direct damage multiplier) - armor damage) and the last modifier is applied to the whole * body damage multiplier Note than none of the values in each step can be negative. If damage < damage minimum (dealt), damage = damage minimum (dealt).

remaining_armor_reduction_example.quote: Orc Warrior takes 27 - 18 (10% of remaining armor) = 9 * 1.5 = 13 damage to hitpoints

armor_destroyed_full_damage.quote: Once the armor is destroyed, the weapon damage applies at 100% to hitpoints.

dazed_damage.note: Dazed status page says -25% damage dealt; see status_effects.dazed.

falling_damage_per_level.quote: The damage equals 10 per level difference.

secondary_ignores_armor.quote: Secondary damage ignores armor (unless it specifically targets it like acid).

weapon_durability_loss_vs_armor.quote: Melee weapon durability is lowered by 3 when it strikes armor that has at least 50 durability remaining

ranged_weapon_durability_per_shot.quote: [[Bows|Bow]] or [[Crossbows|Crossbow]] durability is lowered by 2 with each shot.

bleeding_damage_page.quote: The minimum (hitpoints) damage necessary for the effect to occur at all is 6.

stunned.quote: Someone that is stunned has no zone of control, can't be rotated out and is not contributing to surround bonus.

poison_webknecht.quote: Like bleeding, poison is only applied if 7 or more (hitpoints) damage has been dealt. The spider poison deals 5 damage per turn for 3 turns

states.quote: Morale has six states and represents the mental condition of combatants and their effectiveness in battle.

default_state.quote: Steady is the default state, and non-undead enemies start with it

multipliers_apply_after_additive.quote: They count after additive bonuses from skills, perks and equipment, affecting them as well.

starting_morale_brothers.value: from mood: good mood can start Confident, bad mood lowers max morale
starting_morale_brothers.quote: Brothers' morale depends on their [[mood]]: good mood gives a chance to start with Confident morale, and bad mood lowers the maximum possible level of morale the brother can have.

value: moved to end of turn order
fleeing_effects.quote: If morale drops to Fleeing, the unit cancels its active [[Shieldwall (20 fatigue)|Shieldwall]], [[Spears|Spearwall]], [[Riposte (25 fatigue)|Riposte]] and [[Indomitable (Status Effect)|Indomitable]], is also instantly moved to the end of turn order.

fleeing_no_fight.quote: Fleeing units try to run away from enemies and can't fight or use skills, and even don't fight if surrounded. Player loses control over fleeing brothers.

base_chance.quote: Resolve is the base chance to succeed.

cap.quote: The maximum chance to succeed is 95% (5% chance to fail), but minimum is 0% (always fail).

step.quote: Positive checks raise morale by one level, negative ones lower it by one level, but there are exceptions.

hidden.quote: They are not shown in the combat log.

skipped_over_500.quote: The chance to succeed is more than 500% before it is capped.

positive_cannot_lift_fleeing_to_breaking.quote: Positive check tries to change Fleeing to Breaking (it fails).

struck_threshold_confirm.quote: as opposed to with no penalty and only if at or above 15 points of damage.

xp_value_of_brother.quote: XP value of a brother is 100 + 30 * (his level - 1).

self_rally.value: Fleeing units can rally when not adjacent to enemies
self_rally.quote: Fleeing units can rally on their own when not adjacent to enemies, or if targeted by skills like [[Rally the Troops]] that restore their morale.

rally_the_troops.quote: | +0.4 * user's resolve, but extra -10 * distance if not fleeing | |Can't raise morale above Steady. Fleeing changes to Wavering on success.

rally_skill_page.quote: Triggers a morale check to raise morale of any ally at wavering or worse morale within 4 tiles, with a bonus of 40% of the skill user's [[File:Resolve.png|bottom|25px]] Resolve, and a penalty of -10 per tile of distance, to the roll. It can also rally fleeing allies within the same range at no penalty.

hp_zero.quote: If this attribute falls to 0, the character is killed or "''struck down''".

temp_injury_threshold_range.quote: Injuries have different thresholds comprised between 25% and 60% of maximum hitpoints (see the list for specific values).
